text: ← Advanced contents AVAILABLE CHAPTERS WHAT YOU WILL LEARNSelect the outflow branch of the equation shared with Bondi flow and separate sonic regularity, heating, and outer boundary conditions. Connect to foundations: Why is the Sun’s surface about 6,000 degrees? ↗ Compare solution assumptions and boundary data in the solution library ↗ 01Can a hot atmosphere remain static? In a hot atmosphere such as the solar corona, a pressure gradient pushes gas outward. Begin with Newtonian gravity from a mass M and an isothermal, spherical, steady gas. Magnetic fields, rotation, and electron–ion temperature differences are not yet included. cs² = kBTμmp Here μ is the mean mass per particle in proton-mass units; the example specifies μ = 0.6. This is the isothermal sound speed, so do not insert the heat-capacity ratio used in an adiabatic sound speed. 02Apply mass and momentum conservation to a wind Now define u > 0 as the outward velocity. A steady wind has constant mass-loss rate 4πr²ρu. Eliminating the density gradient yields the same speed equation as in the Bondi chapter; the branch and boundary conditions distinguish the physical flows. Ṁwind = 4πr²ρu (u−cs²u)dudr = 2cs²r−GMr² The right-hand side is negative inside rs and positive outside. On the subsonic branch the left-hand coefficient is also negative, so du/dr can be positive even inside the critical radius. Inward gravity does not forbid outward acceleration: include the pressure gradient in the force budget. 03The smooth accelerating sonic branch rs = GM2cs², x = rrs, 𝓜 = ucs 𝓜²−ln(𝓜²) = 4ln x+4x−3 Connect a subsonic branch at x < 1 to a supersonic branch at x > 1. Expanding numerator and denominator together at the sonic point gives d𝓜/dx = +1, compared with −1 for Bondi’s inward speed. Choosing the wrong branch reverses the physical interpretation. The plot compares the two critical curves. Each point is obtained by bisection of the integrated relation, avoiding a numerical division by zero at the sonic point. 04Why hydrostatic balance can be insufficient The static isothermal equation can also be integrated. Given a base radius r₀ and density ρ₀, its density profile is: ρ(r)ρ₀ = exp[GMcs²(1r−1r₀)] Density tends to a finite nonzero value at infinity. Such a static atmosphere cannot match a sufficiently low-pressure exterior. A confined outer boundary can permit a subsonic breeze, so writing the differential equation alone does not uniquely demand the transonic wind. Critical regularity is important, but heating, base conditions, and the outer connection also matter. Dynamical selection of a stable flow is a larger problem than the steady equations solved here. 05Solar scales and the cost of isothermality For one solar mass, T = 106 K, and μ = 0.6, the isothermal sound speed is about 117 km/s and the sonic point about 6.9 solar radii. Raising temperature moves the sonic point inward as pressure becomes stronger relative to gravity. A velocity profile still leaves density normalization unspecified, so a base density or equivalent boundary condition is needed for mass loss. Expansion requires heating to remain isothermal; this model does not solve an energy equation. At large radius 𝓜² ≈ 4 ln x, so it does not even predict a finite terminal speed. Real solar wind is magnetized, with heating, conduction, and weak collisionality also important. Use Parker flow as a basic transonic outflow model, distinct from a magnetized disk wind extracting rotational angular momentum. CHECK YOUR UNDERSTANDING Pause and work it out. At fixed central mass and mean molecular weight, quadruple the isothermal temperature. How do sound speed and sonic radius change? Does the sonic point alone fix mass loss? Show the answer and reasoning Sound speed doubles because cs ∝ √T; sonic radius decreases by four. The mass-loss rate 4πr²ρu still needs a density normalization, such as a base density. The critical velocity curve alone does not fix it. REFERENCES & PHYSICAL INPUTS Explanations and derivations are written for this guide. References may use different notation or normalization. Panel methods and approximations are stated in the text.
